saṃ:
[upasaggapada.]  CL=10 Meanings of the prefix so/saṃ:
1. Mutual (aññamañña)
2. Visible, apparent (sandissamāna)
3. Existing, present (santa, saṃvijjamāna)
4. Praise (pasaṃsā)
5. Good, beautiful, pure, natural state (sundara-bhāva, sobhana, sukka, pakati)
6. Completion (samiddhi)
7. Well-arisen (sañjāta)
8. Stronger (balavatara)
9. Little, small amount (appaka)
10. Respectfully (sakkacca)
11. Extremely, intensely (suṭṭhutara, daḷha, bhusa)
12. Successive (aparāpara)
13. Moving back and forth, wandering, repetition (saṃsaraṇa, punappuna-kiriyā)
14. Equality, harmony (sama-bhāva)
15. Special (visesa)
16. Brief (saṅkhepa, saṅkhitta)
17. Share (bhoga)
18. Lower portion (adhobhāga)
19. All portions (sabbato-bhāga)
20. In all ways (sabbato, sabbaso, sabbathā)
21. Mode (pakāra)
22. Meeting (saṅgama)
23. Collection (saṅgahaṇa, sampiṇḍana, samodhāna)
24. Together, united (saha, sahita-bhāva)
25. Well, properly (sammā, suṭṭhu)
26. All-around state (samantatta)
27. Connection (saṃyoga)
28. Strong connection (saṃyutta)
29. Relation (sambandha)
30. Turning back (parivattana)
31. Recognition (saññākaraṇa)
32. Always (nicca, nibaddha)
33. Approaching (upasaṅkamana)
34. Beginning (ādi)
35. Present moment (sampati)
36. Causing delight (paritosana)
37. Offering, supporting (pūjā, saṅgaha)
40. Facing towards (abhimukha)
41. Covering (pidhāna)
42. Completeness (samatta-bhāva)
43. Mixing (missana)
44. Knowing (maññanā)
45. Without special meaning (niratthakaṃ, pada-sobhana, padālaṅkāra)
46. Nearness (samīpa)
47. Moving, flowing (saṃsappana)

[ saṃ + khipa + ta.]  CL=7 (1) That which is a brief. (Na) (2) A summarized table of contents or index. (5) saṃkhittasutta, Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.161 (AN4.161), 4.232 (AN4.232), 5.1 (AN5.1), 5.13 (AN5.13); 8.53 (AN8.53), 8.63 (AN8.63). (6) saṃkhittabalasutta, Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.3 (AN7.3). (7) saṃkhittadhanasutta, Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.5 (AN7.5). (8) Saṃkhittūposathasutta.

[ saṅku + kkata = saṅkita + ṇya.]  CL=10 [From ṇya-paccaya sutthu. saṅkita-saṃ. saṅkia, saṅkita-pyā]
1. Saṅkicca Sāmaṇera - The famous novice monk (who became an Arahant with paṭisambhidā knowledge at age 7, as a disciple of Venerable Sāriputta)
2. Saṅkicca - The Bodhisatta (in a previous life)
3. Of Saṅkicca lineage, born in Saṅkicca clan (referring to the ascetic teacher named Kisa)
The story of Saṅkicca Sāmaṇera:
Having accumulated merit under previous Buddhas and developed strong conditions for Nibbāna across many lives, he took rebirth in a wealthy brahmin family in Sāvatthī during our Buddha"s time. His mother died during pregnancy due to illness. When her body was being cremated, the womb remained unburned. People pierced it with bamboo stakes and covered it with embers. Though the womb burned, the golden-colored infant remained alive, as if sleeping on a lotus.
For one in their final birth (pacchimabhavika-satta), even Mount Meru cannot prevent them from attaining Arahantship - death cannot occur before this achievement. The next day, people finding the sleeping infant were amazed that he survived while his mother"s body burned completely. They took him to the village and consulted fortune-tellers.
The fortune-tellers predicted: 'If this child remains a householder, his relatives will suffer poverty for seven generations. If he becomes a monk, he will travel with 500 monk followers.' He was named 'Saṅkicca' because his eye was pierced by a bamboo stake (saṅkunā chinnakkhikoṭitāya Saṅkicco - Thera.Ṭṭha.2.213). This name became well-known. His relatives decided that despite the prediction of poverty, they would have him ordained under Venerable Sāriputta when he grew up..

saṃvara:
[ saṃ + vara + a.]  CL=7 (1) Preventing or blocking (preventing or obstructing unwholesome deeds). (2) Restraining (The practice of restraining). (3) Not committing (abstaining from wrongful actions). (4) Prohibition (the act of forbidding or prohibiting certain actions.) (5) Five Kinds of Dhamma (that support restraint): sīla: morality. sati: mindfulness. ñāṇa: wisdom. khantī: patience. vīriya: effort. these dhammas prevent or block wholesome actions. (6) Paccayapaṭisevana (taking proper use of requisites (supporting conditions)). (7) Ājīvapārisuddhi (purification of livelihood). (8) a person or quality that controls, restrains or holds back unwholesomeness. (9) The boundaries or rules that serve as guidelines for restraint. (10) Nine Aspects of Phalūpacāra Saṃvara Dhammas: A description of qualities or practices associated with restraint: (A) Subharatā: Being easy to support; low maintenance. (B) Suposatā: Being easy to maintain; having minimal needs. (C) Appiccha: Having few desires or wishes. (D) Santuṭṭha: Contentment or satisfaction. (E) Sallekha: Erasing or lessening defilements. (F) Dhuta: Shaking off defilements. (G) Pāsādika: Graceful or pleasing demeanor. (H) Apacaya: Destroying all defilements. (I) Vīriyārambha: Striving or making diligent effort.  (11) A prince named Saṃvara. (12) saṃvarasutta, saṃyutta Nikāya 35.98 (SN35.98) , aṅguttara Nikāya 4.14 (AN4.14). (13) Saṃvarajātaka, jātaka 462 (JA462). (14) The sun named Saṃvara.

saṃvega:
[ saṃ + vijī + ṇa.]  CL=7 (1) Dismay, fear, or trembling of the mind. (A) Wisdom that perceives the danger in continued existence or rebirth. (B) Wisdom arises in conjunction with moral dread (ottappa), a wholesome mental state that motivates ethical conduct by recognizing the consequences of unwholesome actions. (C) Moral dread (ottappa), a wholesome mental quality characterized by a respectful awareness of ethical principles and a concern to avoid wrongdoing. (D) The noble path (ariya magga) leading to liberation. (E) Serenity meditation (samatha) and insight meditation (vipassanābhāvanā). (F) Insight or penetrating wisdom (vipassanā). (G) The path (magga) accompanied by insight (vipassanā). (H) The trembling or anxiety of the mind. (2) The wisdom that is prone to fear, dismay, or trembling. (3) (A) The act of being frightened or dismayed. (B) A cause or reason that induces fear or dismay. (4) A period or instance of fear, dismay, or trembling. (5) That which is to be feared or respected.
[Nīti, dhātu. 48. 224. Dhātvattha. Kaccaya. 623, 640. Saṃ+vija + ṇa. Moga, 5. 154-paucikā. Saṃ + vija + ṇa. Nirutti. 441-nhā. Saṃvijjanaṃ saṃvego. Nirutti. 542-nhā. Saṃvega - saṃ. Saṃvea, saṃvega - prā, addhamāgadhī.]

[ saṃyutta + aṭṭhakathā ]  CL=7 The Commentary on the Saṃyutta Pāḷi (Saṃyuttaṭṭhakathā): This text explains the meaning of the Saṃyutta Pāḷi in detail. It was originally convened and preserved during three Buddhist synods by arahants. The venerable Mahāmahinda brought this text to Sri Lanka, where it was written in the Sinhala language. Later, the venerable Mahābuddhaghosa translated the commentary into the Pāḷi language.
